text:
Alex: heads-up — testing a dynamic sampler reconfig flow for canaries. want to avoid full-span backlog when exporter handshake fails.
Marta: curious — what exactly is failing today?
Alex: if the otlp exporter can't reach collector during a canary rollout, our SDK clients either block on retries or buffer unboundedly. then process OOMs or we drop everything. both bad.
Yusuf: are we talking python/go/rust differences or a platform-level policy?
Alex: both. idea is a small SDK pattern: hot-swap a lightweight delegating sampler at init that can be reconfigured from control-plane. default to conservative sampling for low-pri spans until exporter handshake ok. keep critical traces (error, alloc, rollout) sampled.
Cheng: exporter handshake and shutdown ordering has bitten us before. any change must ensure graceful drain on canary rollback.
Sam: impl sketch: at startup set sampler = DelegatingSampler(ref to atomic config). on canary start, control-plane pushes desired rates. if exporter not ready, set background sample-rate=0.1 and keep tenant-critical attribute-based exceptions at 1.0.
Anita: KV-cache / prefix-cache spans are noisy — safe to throttle them, but we mustn't drop cold-start or latency-regression traces. how do we mark them?
Alex: tag spans with span.kind and a custom attr e.g., "redwood.span_class" = "kvcache|inference|control". control-plane rules -> keep inference errors and cold-starts at full sample.
Yusuf: language specifics? python->opentelemetry-sdk supports a Sampler interface; swapping provider is heavy. better to implement a ForwardingSampler that consults atomic config.
Alex: example python pattern:\n```python\nfrom opentelemetry.sdk.trace.sampling import Sampler, SamplingResult, Decision, SamplingParameters\nfrom threading import Lock\n\nclass DelegatingSampler(Sampler):\n    def __init__(self, ctl):\n        self._ctl = ctl  # atomic config object\n    def should_sample(self, parent_context, trace_id, name, kind, attributes, links):\n        cfg = self._ctl.get()\n        # attr-based rule first\n        if attributes.get("redwood.span_class") == "inference":\n            return SamplingResult(Decision.RECORD_AND_SAMPLE)\n        if cfg.get("background_rate", 0) <= 0:\n            return SamplingResult(Decision.DROP)\n        # fallback to ratio\n        return SamplingResult(Decision.RECORD_AND_SAMPLE if random.random() < cfg.get("background_rate", 0.01) else Decision.DROP)\n    def get_description(self):\n        return "DelegatingSampler"\n```\nCheng: go: same idea but use an atomic.Value pointing to a function or sampler instance. can't rely on global ReplaceProvider at runtime. we wrap sdktrace.Sampler with our dynamic sampler.
Sam: rust is trickier — opentelemetry-rust's Sampler trait can be implemented with an Arc<RwLock<Config>>; pay attention to perf of lock in hot path. RwLock read is fine but avoid blocking in critical path.
Marta: what about buffering/backpressure? if exporter backfills, we still can hit memory spikes. can sampler reconfig help?
Alex: yes — sampler is the first line of defense. also set bounded exporter queue (local cap) + backpressure signal to control-plane. if queue full, immediately lower background_rate to 0.01 and emit a high-prio alert span.
Yusuf: we need consistent semantics across SDKs: 
- delegating sampler default behavior
- control-plane API: /v1/telemetry/sampler?service=svc-inference&canary=true returns json {background_rate:0.01, overrides:[{attr:\"redwood.span_class=error\",rate:1.0}]}
Cheng: include a health-check handshake: exporter init must call collector /handshake and only once we get 200 we flip exporter.ready = true and raise background_rate to target. otherwise keep low.
Anita: test plan?
Alex: unit test sampler wrapper, e2e: start canary, blacklist collector, observe background spans drop, check critical spans still recorded. add chaos test: exporter flaps and ensure sampler toggles without leaking memory.
Sam: small gotcha — OTLP batching exporter may still queue accepted spans even if sampler drops locally; so ensure sampler runs early (before batching) — which is normal. confirm in each SDK.
Marta: ops/observability: add dashboard tile showing sampler config per deployment + exporter queue depth + sampled-span-rate. also track dropped-span-count by reason (sampler vs queue-full).
Cheng: concerning shutdown: ensure SDK drain timeout respects canary rollback timeline. on rollback, we don't want to wait for long drains; instead set sampler to DROP and flush minimal critical spans synchronously.
deploy-bot: deploy svc-inference/canary-2026-03-20 started by @Sam at 2311112245 :rocket:
Alex: noted — during this canary we'll intentionally block collector to validate fallback.
deploy-bot: deploy svc-inference/canary-2026-03-20 finished (status: partial-failure) at 2311112290 :warning:
Marta: can we record the observed stats from that run? queue depth peaked at 48k, mem spike +30% on the canary hosts.
Yusuf: action items:
- implement DelegatingSampler pattern in python/go/rust (owners: Alex/Yusuf/Cheng)
- control-plane sampler endpoint + rule format (owner: Sam)
- dashboard panels: sampler rates, exporter handshake, queue depth, dropped counts (owner: Marta)
- add chaos e2e that flakes collector to validate no OOMs (owner: Anita)
Anita: +1 — i'll add the chaos job to the infra repo and start with a low-risk run.
Alex: i'll open PR w/ python impl and a readme for the sampler rules.
Marta: thanks — this should make canaries much safer. :thumbsup:
